text:
natalie: Hey team, spotted something odd in the new reporting heatmap: the sample counts in the legend don't match the drilldown totals. looks like sampling is applied twice somewhere.

sam: Ugh, saw that too when checking the quantized-8bit run. heatmap shows 120k but drilldown rows sum to 30k.

liam: @natalie could you paste the query or widget config? might be a viz-layer scaling issue or an upstream aggregator bug.

natalie: sure — widget config excerpt: ```SELECT bin, count(*) as cnt FROM eval_runs WHERE run_id IN (<run_list>) GROUP BY bin``` then frontend multiplies by sample_rate from telemetry. not sure where the extra factor comes from.

maya: I reproduced locally. The runner CI export sometimes emits both `sampled_count` and `raw_count` and the dashboard code picks whichever exists. for older runs `sample_rate` was applied at export, new runner applies at ingestion too.

liam: ah nice catch. so double-application between runner exporter and dashboard ingestion. sounds like we need a small migration or a guard in the viz code.

sam: Proposed quick fix: prefer `raw_count` if present and ignore `sample_rate` on that metric; add a warning badge on the widget when schema mismatch detected. low-risk rollback if something breaks.

natalie: agree. I'll open a tiny PR to the dashboard repo to prefer raw_count and surface a telemetry mismatch warning.

maya: Also adding a CI unit for manifest parity would save future surprises — `assert exporter.schema == dashboard.expected_schema` for known runs. I can draft that.

liam: Might also be worth running a diff across recent quantization experiments (8bit vs float16) to catch shifts in aggregate metrics that could hide sampling bugs. e.g., run `tools/eval_diff --metric=coverage --group=bin` across runs.

natalie: PR: https://github.com/redwood/dashboard/pull/1987 — small change + a note in the widget readme.

eval-bot: CI passed for PR 1987 (all unit tests + viz smoke) :white_check_mark:

sam: cool. can we also tag a couple of recent runs that look impacted so CS doesn't freak out? cc @support

maya: I'll annotate runs `run-20240612-q8` and `run-20240615-fp16` with a `sampling_mismatch` label and add a console banner.

natalie: thanks folks. follow-up: I'll run a backfill script to recompute counts for the last 30 days and ping infra if it looks heavy.

liam: 👍 one small note — add an entry to the release notes: "Dashboard — fixed double-sampling in heatmap legends" so PMs can explain to customers.

sam: adding to notes now. thanks! :tada:
